correctness.rationale: Directly solve both scalar impulse decay equations on [0,d) and [d,H], integrate their product and subtract the orders. The contrast factors as a positive prefactor times an affine function of z=exp(-(a+b)(H-d)), with endpoint values E>0 and -D; these give all sharp signs and the unique crossover, including the equal-rate boundary. Small-gap and large-gap limits follow by exact exponential expansions. Actual standalone verifier passed 22813 supplemental assertions; experiments are not relied on to prove the all-parameter theorem.

value.rationale: Equal pulse mass with exchanged quality labels isolates a practical question about pulse quality sequence, not general resource volume. A finite evaluation horizon reverses the better order if and only if quality memory decays faster than activity, with a unique explicit switching time independent of mass and quality contrast. The nonzero zero-gap limiting horizon exposes a singular observational effect; this is a fully classified, motivated two-pulse benchmark useful for distinguishing finite-window versus long-window interpretations in more complex subsidy models. The toy output is not empirical validation.
